question: What does 'class' mean in Python?
answer: 'class' in Python means a blueprint for creating objects [S1] [S3]

citations.text: 6. Object-Oriented Programming A class is a blueprint and an object is an instance of that class. S2.title: Python Glossary Overloaded Terms
S2.text: class: in Python a class is a blueprint for creating objects. It is not a category label as in classification problems. function: a reusable block of code defined with def. It is not necessarily a mathematical function. mode: when opening a file the mode string such as "r", "w" or "a" says how the file is used. statistics.mode(data) is a different thing: it returns the most frequent value. sample: random.sample(population, k) draws k unique elements without replacement. It has nothing to do with a statistical sample unless you use it to build one. normal: random.gauss(mu, sigma) and random.normalvariate(mu, sigma) draw numbers from a normal distribution. seed: random.seed(n) makes the random sequence reproducible, so a program prints the same random numbers on every run. iterable: an object you can loop over, such as a list or string.
